text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - Pakistan bought 225,000 tonnes of Australian wheat during its weekend tender and no U.S. wheat, U.S. exporters said. Price details were not available early Monday, but shipment was expected for December.

- Bangladesh bought 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat for December shipment during its weekend tender for 200,000 tonnes, said U.S. exporters. Prices were unavailable. One exporter said the wheat will likely come from Australia.
WHEAT SALES - Bulgaria bought 120,000 tonnes of Argentine soft wheat at $168.75 per tonne cost and freight, European grain traders said Monday. The wheat is for shipment in December.
SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea is to tender for 55,000 tonnes of No.1 soybeans Wednesday for December-January shipment.

WHEAT TENDERS - Turkey will invite bids December 10 to import 200,000 tonnes of red and white milling wheat on a three-year credit basis, a grain official said. He said the imports would be from either the United States, Australia, Argentina or any European Union member country.

WHEAT TENDERS - Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender Wednesday for 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said. Shipment would be from the Pacific Northwest. The tender is on behalf of Taiwan wheat companies including President Enterprise, Tai Yu Products, Chia Hsin, Formosa Oilseed and Lien Hwa Industry.

BARLEY TENDER - Cyprus has invited tenders to buy 25,000 tonnes of feed barley for shipment in December 1996 or January 1997. Tenders close on December 3, a statement from the Cyprus Grain Commission said.
LENTIL TENDER - Syria offered 9,500 tonnes of lentils for export. December 16 was set as final date for bids and results would be announced on December 17.

MARKET TALK - U.S. grain inspected for export during the week ended November 28: soybeans 35.321 million bushels vs 32.246 million the previous week, wheat 16.367 million vs 16.513 million, corn 48.898 million vs 55.563 million, sorghum 5.423 million vs 4.552 million, oats nils, and barley nil vs 1.402 million.

MARKET TALK - Croatia will export some 100,000 tonnes of maize, the state news agency Hina quoted Agriculture Minister Matej Jankovic as saying. It said Croatia had a surplus of between 300,000 and 400,000 tonnes of maize after an excellent 1996 harvest...Yugoslavia could export up to two million tonnes of maize from its 1996 crop, an official of the country's Fund for Grains said. "Our surplus is about one million tonnes," director of the fund Vukosav Sakovic told Reuters. "But due to a sharp drop in head of cattle, we will have two instead of one million tonnes of maize for exports.".

MARKET TALK - Moscow's grain trade is casting its eyes as near as Kazakhstan and as far as Argentina in search of cheap supplies to make up for Russia's second poor harvest in a row, trade sources said. They also said that while domestic farmers had understated actual 1996 output by as much as 10 percent, Russia still had one of its worst harvests in three decades, with short supplies of high-quality bread-making wheat... Algeria's grain office on Monday denied trade reports that it seeks to import 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat.
